measuresOfCentralTendency.title: Measures of Central Tendency
measuresOfCentralTendency.description: Describe the center of a data set.

measures.name: Mean
measures.description: The average: add all values and divide by number of values.

measures.name: Median
measures.description: The middle value after data is arranged from lowest to highest.
measures.sensitivity: NOT affected by outliers - better for skewed data.

measures.name: Mode
measures.sensitivity: A dataset can have no mode, one mode, or multiple modes (bimodal).

variation.title: Measures of Variation
variation.description: Show how spread out data is from the center.

measures.name: Range
measures.description: Difference between highest and lowest values.

measures.name: Standard Deviation
measures.description: Measures how spread out data is from the mean.
measures.small: Data points clustered close to the mean.
measures.large: Data points more spread out from the mean.

types.name: Normal Distribution (Bell Curve)
types.description: Mean, median, and mode are all at the center.
types.empiricalRule: 68% within ±1 SD | 95% within ±2 SD | 99.7% within ±3 SD

types.name: Positively Skewed
types.description: Tail extends to the RIGHT. A few extremely HIGH scores pull the mean UP.
types.relationship: Mode < Median < Mean (mean is pulled toward the tail).
types.example: Income distribution: most people earn moderate amounts, but a few billionaires pull the mean up.

types.name: Negatively Skewed
types.description: Tail extends to the LEFT. A few extremely LOW scores pull the mean DOWN.
types.relationship: Mean < Median < Mode (mean is pulled toward the tail).
types.example: Easy test scores: most score high, but a few very low scores pull the mean down.

types.name: Bimodal Distribution
types.description: Has TWO peaks instead of one, suggesting two common values in the dataset.

percentileRank.title: Percentile Rank
percentileRank.description: The percentage of scores that fall at or below a particular score.
percentileRank.example: If you score in the 90th percentile, you scored as well as or better than 90% of test-takers.
percentileRank.warning: Percentile rank is NOT the same as percentage correct.

regressionToTheMean.title: Regression Toward the Mean
regressionToTheMean.description: As more data is collected, outliers (very high or very low results) are followed by results closer to the average.
regressionToTheMean.example: A basketball player who scores 50 points one game is likely to score closer to their average in the next game.
regressionToTheMean.implication: Extreme performances tend to be followed by more typical ones.

effectSizeVsSignificance.title: Effect Size vs Statistical Significance
effectSizeVsSignificance.warning: Two concepts students frequently mix up on the AP exam. They measure DIFFERENT things.

effectSize.definition: Indicates the strength of the relationship between variables (non-experimental) or the size of the difference between groups (experimental).
effectSize.question: HOW BIG is the effect?

statisticalSignificance.definition: Indicates that the results are not likely due to chance and instead are likely due to the variables being studied.
statisticalSignificance.question: Is the effect REAL (not due to chance)?

effectSizeVsSignificance.keyDistinction: A study can be statistically significant (p < 0.05) but have a SMALL effect size. This means the result is real but the practical impact is minimal.
effectSizeVsSignificance.example: A therapy study finds p = 0.01 (significant) but d = 0.15 (small effect). The therapy works, but the improvement is very modest.

correlationConcepts.title: Correlation

interpretations.label: Strong positive
interpretations.meaning: As X increases, Y strongly tends to increase.

interpretations.label: Moderate positive
interpretations.meaning: As X increases, Y tends to increase.

interpretations.label: Weak positive
interpretations.meaning: Slight tendency for both to increase together.

interpretations.label: Weak negative
interpretations.meaning: Slight tendency for one to decrease as other increases.

interpretations.label: Moderate negative
interpretations.meaning: As X increases, Y tends to decrease.

interpretations.label: Strong negative
interpretations.meaning: As X increases, Y strongly tends to decrease.

correlationConcepts.criticalRule: Correlation does NOT equal causation. Third variable problem: a third unmeasured variable may influence both.
correlationConcepts.scatterplotInterpretation: Points clustered tightly along a line = strong correlation. Points scattered widely = weak correlation.
